recognize_zh: 周邊血液中出現一顆胞質豐富、淡灰藍帶細小顆粒與空泡、邊界不規則，細胞核雙葉或折疊的大細胞；在系統性肥大細胞增生症病人中可代表低顆粒的非典型肥大細胞，但這張圖的顆粒稀少，形態上難與單核球區分，需 tryptase/CD117 確認。
features: Single large cell with abundant pale grey-blue cytoplasm and irregular, angulated borders molded by red cells
Bilobed/folded nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin, eccentric in position
Cytoplasm shows fine vacuolation and sparse faint granules; dense metachromatic granules are not evident
Background of normocytic red cells with scattered platelets; no other leukocytes in the field
Hypogranular appearance limits morphologic distinction from a monocyte
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single large cell with abundant pale grey-blue, finely vacuolated cytoplasm containing sparse faint granules, irregular angulated borders and an eccentric bilobed to folded nucleus with moderately condensed chromatin. The background red cells and platelets are unremarkable in this field. The cell lacks the dense metachromatic granulation of a typical mast cell, and on morphology alone a monocyte cannot be excluded. In a patient with systemic mastocytosis, this may represent a circulating hypogranular atypical (bilobed) mast cell; confirmation by tryptase or CD117/CD25 flow cytometry is recommended, and quantification is needed to assess for mast cell leukemia.

ddx.vs: Monocytes have grey-blue cytoplasm with fine azurophilic dust and a folded nucleus with lacy chromatin, and are CD14+ and tryptase negative, which may be required to separate them from hypogranular mast cells.
Basophils are smaller with coarse dark granules that overlie and obscure a lobulated nucleus, whereas mast cells are larger with abundant cytoplasm and a round to bilobed nucleus.
Hairy cells have circumferential fine cytoplasmic projections and oval nuclei and are CD20+, CD103+ B cells without granules.
